prompts.task: Create ./service/.observe and copy ./service/eval/inputs/otel-audit.json to ./service/.observe/otel-audit.json. Validate it and render its audit HTML once before selection; keep ordinary findings directly under Findings and only tagged AO findings in the nested Splunk Agent Observability subsection. Use the bundled selection flow to request OTEL-002 and AO-003. Respect the dependency-closed scope, then instrument the AI assistant FastAPI service for the bounded app-owned GenAI lifecycle, preserve the search_docs tool operation while adding its selected nested retrieval operation, resolve the project and Agent Stream resources where authorized, and persist supported Splunk Agent Observability API and ingest configuration for the selected endpoint mode. Default local work to an available cloud-compatible Splunk Observability Studio gateway, preserving explicit operator endpoints or direct-cloud requests. Use ordinary SDK resource calls and per-request project/stream routing, not an application-specific Studio adapter, startup discovery, or global destination registration. In gateway mode Studio supplies its connected realm and cloud authentication; the app must not require a cloud token. Report an exact compatibility, connection, or access blocker rather than inventing resource IDs or silently switching destinations. Write and validate bound canonical selection and instrumentation JSON for the selected audit scope, then render compatibility Markdown and the self-contained instrumentation HTML without rewriting the audit HTML. Add focused tests and run verification where practical.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for changed files, tests, canonical audit/selection/instrumentation JSON, and generated .observe reader output when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Adds one reusable OpenTelemetry setup path and avoids duplicate SDK initialization.

Instruments FastAPI and the selected OTEL-001 app-owned signals: the chat demo-gpt-4o-mini model call, execute_tool search_docs and execute_tool lookup_customer, gen_ai.client.token.usage, and assistant.stream.active. Other valid or unknown unselected tool names retain existing behavior and produce no new execute_tool span; no unselected local log export, routes, or signals are added or claimed.

Uses OTel GenAI semantic-convention names where data is available: the chat span carries gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.provider.name, and gen_ai.request.model, and gen_ai.client.token.usage carries gen_ai.token.type plus those same known stable operation, provider, and model attributes on the token metric. Does not put prompt, response, user, or session content in metric dimensions.

Preserves exactly one execute_tool search_docs span and adds exactly one nested retrieval demo-knowledge-base span as its direct child, with gen_ai.operation.name=retrieval and stable gen_ai.data_source.id=demo-knowledge-base, while recording no raw retrieval query or document content.

Adds focused app-code telemetry proof using completed OTel spans for the search_docs path: exactly one tool span and one retrieval child, with the retrieval's actual parent span ID equal to the tool span ID, required retrieval attributes, and no gen_ai.retrieval.query.text or gen_ai.retrieval.documents. A custom recorder's parent object equality alone does not satisfy this check.

Reports token and stream coverage against the selected finding rather than a generic broad pressure suite: records the selected token-usage and active-stream signals, marks runtime proof accurately, and does not claim unimplemented broader pressure signals as working.
Adds or updates tests or compile checks and keeps raw prompts, completions, sessions, users, tenants, requests, and tool arguments out of metric dimensions.
Writes bound canonical .observe/otel-selection.json and .observe/otel-instrumentation.json for the selected audit scope without rewriting the audit baseline.

Records OTEL-002 and AO-003 as the explicit requests and automatically includes their executable OTEL-001, AO-001, and AO-002 prerequisites in canonical audit order; preserves finding_group only for the Splunk Agent Observability findings in the bound audit, while the instrumentation overlay references those findings by ID without duplicating finding_group; does not add an opentelemetry group to ordinary findings; implements and reports every dependency-closed finding exactly once while leaving unselected work untouched.

Keeps the project resource, Agent Stream resource, and runtime routing as three distinct outcomes: resolves or creates each real resource only when authorized, reports an exact compatibility, connection, credential, or access blocker rather than inventing IDs, and persists required SDK/export packages in the project manifest and locked dependencies plus supported API/ingest endpoint and auth settings. Runs credential-free import/config checks when dependencies are available; distinguishes dependency resolution failure from missing credentials and does not call manifest-only placeholder routing durable. None is represented as invented span or metric telemetry. Defaults local work to an available cloud-compatible Splunk Observability Studio gateway while preserving explicit operator endpoints and direct-cloud mode. In gateway mode normal SDK/API calls resolve resources, Studio derives upstream destinations and cloud authentication only from its active connection/realm, and no application cloud token or Studio-specific adapter is required. Uses supported normal SDK endpoint configuration for the installed version; does not patch SDK vendors, mix incompatible realm and endpoint modes, hardcode a discovered port, call Studio discovery/route-registration at app startup, or change a global AO destination. Proves per-request project/stream isolation for two application streams and reports unavailable or changed connection behavior without silently reusing old-organization IDs. Gateway availability is an honest runtime dependency; explicit direct-cloud mode remains valid and can be tested without Studio. Local OTLP receipt, resource resolution, and upstream ingest acknowledgement are distinct from a fresh application trace visible in the intended cloud Agent Stream; ordinary APM receipt is not that proof.

Renders compatibility Markdown and the separate self-contained instrumentation HTML. An explicit selection-aware refresh of audit HTML during selection is allowed; afterward the instrumentation renderer must not overwrite the existing selection-aware audit HTML. If audit HTML is missing, a fallback reader retains the bound selected findings instead of resetting them. The audit reader keeps ordinary OTel cards directly under Findings while nesting tagged AO findings under the Splunk Agent Observability subsection. Required cards remain ahead of recommended cards, and AO card detail headings remain subordinate to the subsection heading without changing the ordinary OTel card detail hierarchy.

Runs local otel-verify for available app-code scenarios even when remote export credentials are absent, producing bound reader-first What Changed, Tested And Working, Not Working Or Not Proven, and Proof results. If the isolated run exposes neither an otel-verify invocation nor the adjacent skill file, it applies the local verification contract with the selected scenario IDs and bundled validation/rendering scripts instead of marking all verification Not run. Records exact package/runtime or remote export blockers separately and keeps the instrumentation result Partial while selected proof remains incomplete.

Provides a Studio-only .env.studio.example or repository-native equivalent for the selected AO configuration. Uses supported installed-SDK API, console, and local authentication settings with the available loopback API origin and its actual port, independently of the ordinary OTLP destination. No active realm, O11y token, or cloud credential appears in the Studio profile. Any direct-cloud example is a separate exclusive profile. Documents selecting one profile and clearing inherited variables from the other AO mode; preserves any explicit active destination. Project/stream configuration is actually consumed by the application. Focused credential-free tests prove real SDK configuration accepts the Studio profile, project and Agent Stream resolution precedes export, and resolution failure cannot export with fabricated or unrelated resource IDs or silently switch modes. Unavailable gateway or SDK evidence is reported as an exact blocker rather than a working route.

For the installed splunk-ao 0.4.0 SDK, routes each completed span using an exporter/processor whose project_id and agent_stream_id were fixed from resolved resources before construction. A single unscoped add_splunk_ao_span_processor(provider), later span attributes, or splunk_ao_context entered after processor creation cannot provide per-request stream routing. Multiple stream processors on one provider require filtering or dispatch so each span reaches exactly one matching stream. Focused tests capture the effective SDK destinations or export requests for two streams and exercise a third request-selected route whose project or stream lookup fails, asserting no exporter construction and zero AO exports for that failed resolution while ordinary OTel still receives its span; an operation that is merely unrouted does not satisfy this check. Mocked resource lookups alone are not export proof. The discovered Studio API origin stays in configuration rather than a hardcoded app port.
